hero.name: KyuTae Hwang
hero.summary: PhD student and computational cancer immunology researcher studying how systemic and intratumoral immune states shape response to immunotherapy, with a focus on longitudinal single-cell genomics, T-cell receptor biology, and spatial tumor–immune organization.

profile.institution: City of Hope · Irell & Manella Graduate School of Biological Sciences
profile.methods: Single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, clinical cohort analysis

about.headline: I study immunotherapy response as a dynamic, multi-compartment immune-system problem.
about.text: My work connects peripheral blood and tumor immune states to identify cellular programs, clonal behavior, and spatial organization associated with treatment response. I am especially interested in translational questions where high-dimensional genomic measurements can be distilled into biologically interpretable and clinically testable signals.

researchThemes.label: Systemic response
researchThemes.title: Early peripheral immune dynamics
researchThemes.text: Characterizing early on-treatment T/NK-cell changes and signaling programs in peripheral blood and asking how these dynamics relate to later clinical response.

researchThemes.label: T-cell biology
researchThemes.title: Cell state, clonotype, and treatment outcome
researchThemes.text: Integrating transcriptional states with TCR clonotypes to study expansion, persistence, cross-compartment relationships, and response-associated exhausted CD8 T-cell programs.

researchThemes.label: Tumor ecosystem
researchThemes.title: Spatial myeloid–T-cell organization
researchThemes.text: Studying how macrophage and T-cell programs are arranged within renal cell carcinoma and how local tissue architecture associates with immunotherapy phenotypes.

selectedWork.label: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma
selectedWork.title: Early peripheral T-cell dynamics and pretreatment intratumoral stress-adapted exhausted T cells
paragraphs: Longitudinal single-cell multi-omics profiling of paired tumor and peripheral blood samples from patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma treated with immune checkpoint inhibitor–based therapy.

The study integrates scRNA-seq, scTCR-seq, independent cohort validation, and spatial transcriptomics to examine early peripheral T/NK-cell activation, an ATF3-linked stress-adapted exhausted CD8 T-cell program, clonotype dynamics, and macrophage–T-cell niches.
selectedWork.citation: Hwang K, et al. Early peripheral T cell dynamics and pretreatment intratumoral stress-adapted exhausted T cells associated with ICI response in metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
selectedWork.journalText: Manuscript under revision at Nature Communications.
